headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network tools make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline and Continue both share state via filesystem and can read/write workspace files, so one agent can ingest the other’s outputs through files by default. Cline also uses MCP and browser tools, increasing the chance that untrusted content is treated as instructions. This is not fully isolated, but the bridge is indirect rather than a guaranteed raw-instruction channel.
conditions: IF either agent writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace file and the other agent reads it as instructions, injection is possible.
IF an MCP server returns untrusted content without provenance markers, either agent may follow it.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable MCP servers that return untrusted text.
Add a manual review step before either agent consumes files written by the other.
Prefix shared files with machine-readable provenance headers.
requires-engineering: enforce content provenance filtering in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read and write workspace files, and both touch source code; Cline additionally captures browser screenshots and has broad network egress. That creates a default pathway for sensitive code or editor content to flow between them through the shared filesystem, with possible exfiltration if either agent forwards context to its model provider or MCP server.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, both agents can access them.
IF either agent sends file contents to a remote model provider or MCP server, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Use separate repositories or workspaces.
Store secrets outside the shared workspace.
Disable remote model providers for sensitive sessions.
Restrict MCP servers to local-only endpoints.
requires-engineering: add per-file access controls or redaction before model upload.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write to the same workspace and both support multiple instances with shared state via filesystem. Cline can modify git state and Continue can write workspace files, so concurrent edits can collide and corrupt code or repository state without locking. The overlap is present in default configurations and can cause irreversible git/worktree damage.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same file or branch concurrently, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF one agent commits or rewrites git state while the other is editing, repository corruption or lost work can occur.
mitigations: Run only one agent per workspace at a time.
Use separate git branches per agent.
Enable file locking or a merge queue.
Review diffs before any commit or rewrite.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can act on MCP/tool outputs and Cline can browse and use MCP, so one agent’s output can become the other’s input without a guaranteed verification step. Neither profile shows a built-in cross-agent fact-checking mechanism, so mistaken code, citations, or instructions can propagate into downstream edits or actions. The pathway exists by default but is not inherently autonomous.
conditions: IF one agent writes an incorrect plan or patch into a shared file, the other may reuse it without verification.
IF either agent is allowed to execute tool calls based on the other’s output, errors can cascade into actions.
mitigations: Require human review of inter-agent handoffs.
Add a checksum or schema validation step for shared artifacts.
Keep one agent read-only when the other is acting.
Use explicit task boundaries and handoff notes.
requires-engineering: implement automated verification between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source coding assistants with user-chosen model providers, so there is no documented residency or certification mismatch in the profiles themselves. The main compliance risk is operational: source code and browser screenshots in Cline, plus source code and editor buffers in Continue, may be routed to different providers with different retention policies. The profiles do not prove a breach, so this stays low.
conditions: IF the operator routes either agent to a provider with stricter residency or retention rules than the other, policy mismatch can occur.
IF regulated data is placed in browser screenshots or editor buffers and sent to a remote provider, compliance obligations may be triggered.
mitigations: Use the same approved provider for both agents.
Avoid regulated data in shared workspaces.
Review provider retention settings before use.
Disable browser-based workflows for sensitive projects.
requires-engineering: add policy-aware routing and retention enforcement.
